 Centre makes petrol exports duty-free, hikes diesel export duty to Rs 11.5 per litre 
 The revised rates come amid periodic government reviews of fuel export duties introduced in March 2026 to safeguard domestic supplies.
 Statesman News Service | New Delhi | October 31, 2026 5:26 pm 
 15 April 2020 
 8 mins read -->
 -->
 -->
 Image credit- Canva 
 The Centre has removed the special additional excise duty (SAED) on petrol exports while increasing the export levies on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF). The revised rates were announced through notifications issued by the Ministry of Finance and came into effect on October 31 after being published in the Official Gazette.
 According to the IANS report, under the new structure, petrol exports will no longer attract any special additional excise duty. In contrast, the levy on high-speed diesel exports has been increased by Rs 3 per litre, from Rs 8.5 to Rs 11.5. The duty on aviation turbine fuel has also been raised from Rs 10.5 to Rs 11 per litre.
 Advertisement
 New Export Duty Rates For Petrol, Diesel And ATF 
 Advertisement 
 According to the latest notification issued by the Department of Revenue, the government has reduced the SAED on petrol exports from Rs 2.5 per litre to zero. This effectively removes the export levy on petrol.
 However, diesel exports will now attract a higher duty of Rs 11.5 per litre against the earlier Rs 8.5 per litre. Similarly, the export duty on aviation turbine fuel has been increased by 50 paise per litre, taking it to Rs 11.
 The changes have been notified through separate government orders. The revised duty on ATF is mentioned in Notification No. 56/2026-Central Excise. All the new rates became effective on October 31.
 Why Did The Government Introduce Export Duties? 
 The Centre first introduced special export levies on petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel on March 27, 2026, amid rising tensions in West Asia and concerns over disruptions in global energy supplies.
 The move was aimed at ensuring enough petroleum products remained available in the domestic market. At the time, uncertainty over international oil supplies and fluctuations in global energy prices had raised concerns about the availability of fuel in India.
 By imposing duties on exports, the government sought to discourage excessive overseas sales and ensure that more fuel remained available for domestic consumption.
 Government Reviews Export Duties Every 15 Days 
 The export duty rates have undergone several changes since their introduction in March. The Centre reviews the levies every 15 days based on average international prices of crude oil, petrol, diesel and aviation turbine fuel during the period.
 These reviews allow the government to adjust duties according to changes in global energy prices and market conditions.
 In the previous revision, which came into effect on October 16, the export duty was fixed at Rs 2.5 per litre for petrol, Rs 8.5 per litre for diesel and Rs 10.5 per litre for ATF. The latest revision has now removed the levy on petrol while increasing the duties on diesel and aviation fuel.
